timeline.event: The Coast Salish woolly dog lineage diverged from other dogs, according to ancient genomic analysis.
Mutton, a Coast Salish woolly dog, died; his pelt was later sent to the Smithsonian and analyzed in 2023.
The US Dog and Cat Protection Act (19 U.S.C. 1308) prohibited importing, exporting and selling dog and cat fur products.
Regulation (EC) No 1523/2007 banned trade in cat and dog fur in the EU.
A study in Science combining ancient genomics and Coast Salish knowledge found Mutton had about 85% precolonial woolly dog ancestry.

timeline.event: EFSA held a stakeholder meeting in May and received 922 submissions in a public consultation on live harvesting of goose feathers.
EFSA adopted its scientific opinion on harvesting feathers from live geese on 27 October.
The Responsible Down Standard, which prohibits live plucking and force-feeding, launched in January under Textile Exchange.
A down processor reported an audited processing footprint of about 0.48 kg CO2e per kg, against an EU database value of about 4.15 including bird raising.

timeline.event: The Lacey Act barred interstate transport of birds taken in violation of state law, but poorly enforced it did little to slow the plume trade.
The Weeks-McLean Law effectively ended the US plume trade for millinery.
The Migratory Bird Treaty Act made it a crime to take or sell migratory birds or their parts, including feathers.
A New Zealand study found new synthetic pillows accumulated much more dust mite allergen than new feather pillows over 12 months.
Follow-up work linked the difference mainly to the tighter weave of feather pillow covers.
A review of non-food industrial uses of poultry feathers noted poor thermoplasticity and hard-to-dissolve keratin as barriers.

timeline.event: A comparison of commercial silks found eri and other non-mulberry fibers more extensible than Bombyx mori silk, tied to beta-sheet content and orientation.
Umden-Diwon was recognized as Meghalaya's first eri silk village.
Work on the castor silkworm examined its dietary adaptations when transferred to an ancestral host plant.
Meghalaya's hand-spun, handwoven Ryndia eri textile received a geographical indication tag.
A horizontally acquired gene was shown to mediate red cocoon pigmentation in the eri silkmoth.

timeline.event: Bhagalpur silk from Bihar, a tasar-weaving center, received geographical indication status.
SSR marker analysis documented substantial genetic variation among ecoraces of the tropical tasar silkworm Antheraea mylitta.
A comparative study found tasar and other non-mulberry silks more extensible than Bombyx mori silk.
A review surveyed silk proteins of the Chinese oak tasar silkworm Antheraea pernyi for biomaterial use.
